title: BOHATY DEVELOPMENT Replat No. 2, Geotechnical Peer Review
text: Geotechnical Report Discussion Bohaty Planned Development Medina Township Meeting: App. No.: Applicant: Owners: Engineer: Parcels: Site Area: November 4, 2026 026-2026 R Pride One Construction OH Medina Stonegate LLC Davey Resource Group 026-06C-17-027 76.7615 acres Sublots: Block: Zoning: Utilities: School: Reviewers: 74 B UR Urban Residential Central water and sanitary sewer Medina City Denise Testa EXECUTIVE SUMMARY At the October 2026 Medina County Planning Commission (MCPC) meeting, the MCPC Approved with Modifications the Bohaty Replat No. 2 pending completion of the CTL Conclusions outlined in the Geotechnical Peer Review dated October 19, 2026. For MCPC consideration, the attached analysis addresses the shallower groundwater/seepage conditions identified in the CTL peer review for Sublots 20/21. The MCPC requested confirmation whether the proposed slope modifications and building locations continue to provide the appropriate factors of safety. RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE At the October 2026 MCPC meeting, CTL identified a groundwater/seepage condition that was not incorporated into the Wertz slope stability model. Specifically, the Wertz analysis modeled a piezometric line at elevation 900.0, while the B-15 and B-16 boring logs documented moist to wet soils at approximately elevations 911.0 to 915.5. CTL therefore recommended that Wertz re-evaluate the slope stability with the shallower groundwater/seepage conditions included in the model and resubmit the analysis for review. Wertz Engineering submitted the attached report dated October 13, 2026, and CTL completed a Peer Review on October 19, 2026. DPS Recommendation: Planning Services agrees with CTL's conclusion that further evaluation is unnecessary. Staff recommend that the Planning Commission accept and approve the Bohaty Planned Development Replat No. 2 conclusions of the geotechnical peer review prepared by CTL Engineering, dated October 19, 2026, and require compliance with the revised slope stability recommendations provided by Wertz Geotechnical Engineering, dated October 13, 2026. The recommendations include regrading the backyards of Sublots 20 and 21 to reduce the soil mass along the ravine crown, maintaining the recommended setbacks for the homes and foundations, and directing stormwater away from the ravine. An experienced geotechnical engineer shall be present during construction to observe the regrading and make any necessary adjustments based on actual site conditions. CTL has reviewed the revised slope stability analyses and concurs with the proposed approach and recommendations. Attachments: Bohaty Replat No. 2 Wertz Geotechnical Engineering Slope Stability Analysis-October 13, 2026 CTL Engineering Peer Review-October 19, 2026 Dept. of Planning Services Page 2 of 2 November 4, 2026 Pride One Construction 2211 Medina Road Suite 100 Medina, OH 44256 October 13, 2026 Attention: Ben Weinerman RE: Bohaty Property (Stonegate Subdivision), Lots 20 & 21, Calistoga Circle, Medina Township, Medina County, Ohio; WGE #20251060 Mr. Weinerman: The Medina County Department of Planning Services recommended that a slope stability analysis be performed for Lots 20 and 21 of the subject subdivision. The rear slope behind the homes is approximately 55 feet high with an overall inclination of 2.5:1 (horizontal:vertical). The Rocky River is located at the toe of the slope. The hummocky slope surface of the ravine indicates shallow, historic slope failures. The upper 15 to 20 feet of the ravine is steeper, at approximately a 2:1 grade. A subsurface evaluation for the development was performed by WGE with a report of our findings sent to Ben Weinerman of Pride One Construction on April 23rd, 2025. Test Borings B15 and B-16 were performed near the slope on Lots 20 and 21. The subsurface conditions at Boring B-16 & B-18 mostly encountered stiff to very stiff, brown to gray, lean clay. A soft to medium stiff clay layer was encountered in Boring B-15 in the 33.5 to 35.0 feet sampling interval. A loose silt with minor clay was encountered in Boring B-16 in the 33.5 to 35.0 feet sampling intervals. The stability of the existing slope was evaluated using the program Geostase by Gregory Geotechnical Software. Slope stability was calculated using the Spencer Method at specified boundaries (defined arc entry and exit points along the slope surface). The soil shear strength parameters were estimated from field and lab data. See attached slope evaluation package for details. The following summary of our analysis is provided below: • Existing Conditions: The calculated factory of safety (FS) for potential slope failure affecting the backyard area is approximately 1.2. • Proposed Regrading: Additional analyses were performed to evaluate the effects of lowering and reshaping the crown of the ravine. The modeled profiles included cuts of approximately 5 feet to reduce the soil weight along the crown by approximately 20,000 lbs. per linear foot. The results indicate that regrading the crown with a 5-foot cut would Page 1 Stonegate Lots 20& 21 WGE: 20251060 increase the FS for the backyard slope to be greater than 1.3, while the FS for the potential slope failure affecting the home would be approximately 1.5 • For this evaluation, a minimum FS of 1.3 is required for slopes not supporting structures, while 1.5 is required for slopes supporting structures. CONCLUSION Based on the results of our analyses, we recommend re-grading the backyards of Lots 20 and 21 to reduce the soil mass along the crown of the ravine and improve slope stability. The crown should be lowered to Elevation 941, corresponding to an approximate cut depth of 5 feet, over a distance extending from approximately 100 feet south of the common property line between Lots 19 and 20 to approximately 20 feet north of the common property line between Lots 21 and 22. The regraded surface should rise westward away from the ravine at a maximum grade of 8H:1V. The finish grades of the backyard should be field verified by our personnel. As indicated in our engineering letter dated July 16, 2026, the home should be located 35 feet from the existing crown of the ravine. The foundations should be set back at least 50 feet from the slope face, measured horizontally at the foundation bearing elevation. The storm water from home and impermeable surfaces areas should be directed away from the ravine. We hope you will find this report satisfactory. Please contact our office if we can be of further service or you have questions regarding this submittal. Respectfully submitted, Leroy Wertz, P.E. (CTL) has completed the peer review of the Letter prepared by Wertz Geotechnical Engineering, Inc. (Wertz) and dated October 13, 2026, which was prepared is in response to CTL’s letter dated September 29, 2026. Project Description The project site is located northeast of the intersection of Ledgewood Drive and Sacramento Blvd in Medina Township, Medina County, Ohio. It is our understanding that the site is planned to be parceled into several sublots for single family homes. The purpose of this peer review is to determine if the recommendations provided in the Wertz letter would yield an acceptable factor of safety for the steep slopes behind Lots 20 and 21. Summary of Salient Content Letter by Wertz The letter contained the following statement in the 2nd paragraph on Page 1: Test borings B-15 and B-16 were performed near the slope on Lots 20 and 21. The subsurface conditions at Boring B-16 & B-18 mostly encountered stiff to very stiff, brown to gray, lean clay. CTL believes that the second sentence above should read “…B-15 & B-16…” instead of “… B-16 & B-18…”. CTL Project No. 26051110COR October 19, 2026 Page 2 The letter contained the following statement in the last bullet point on Page 1 (continuing on Page 2): Proposed Regrading: Additional analyses were performed to evaluate the effects of lowering and reshaping the crown of the ravine. The modeled profiles included cuts of approximately 5 feet to reduce the soil weight along the crown by approximately 20,000 lbs. per linear foot. The results indicate that regrading the crown with a 5-foot cut would increase the FS for the backyard slope to be greater than 1.3, while the FS for the potential slope failure affecting the home would be approximately 1.5 The letter contained the following statements in the Conclusion on Page 2: Based on the results of our analyses, we recommend re-grading the backyards of Lots 20 and 21 to reduce the soil mass along the crown of the ravine and improve slope stability. The crown should be lowered to Elevation 941, corresponding to an approximate cut depth of 5 feet, over a distance extending from approximately 100 feet south of the common property line between Lots 19 and 20 to approximately 20 feet north of the common property line between Lots 21 and 22. The regraded surface should rise westward away from the ravine at a maximum grade of 8H:1V. The finish grades of the backyard should be field verified by our personnel. As indicated in our engineering letter dated July 16, 2026, the home should be located 35 feet from the existing crown of the ravine. The foundations should be set back at least 50 feet from the slope face, measured horizontally at the foundation bearing elevation. The storm water from home and impermeable surfaces areas should be directed away from the ravine. CTL Conclusions CTL reviewed the revised slope stability analyses provided by Wertz in their letter dated October 13, 2026. CTL agrees with the approach performed by Wertz, and in CTL’s opinion, the soil parameters are reasonable for the conditions shown in the test borings and observed at the site. The revised analysis was modeled with a groundwater level at a higher elevation as recommended in CTL’s letter dated September 29, 2026. CTL agrees with the revised analysis. CTL also agrees with the revised recommendations provided by Wertz in the Conclusion section of their letter dated October 13, 2026. CTL recommends that an experienced geotechnical engineer is present during construction to observe the regrading of the slope recommended in the Wertz letter, and to make any adjustments to the grading based on the actual site conditions during construction. CTL Project No. 26051110COR October 19, 2026 Page 3 Closing The evaluations, conclusions, and recommendations in this letter are based on our interpretation of the field data obtained during the exploration, our understanding of the project and our experience with similar sites and subsurface conditions using generally accepted geotechnical engineering practices. In the event that changes in the project are proposed, additional information becomes available, or if it is apparent that subsurface conditions are different from those provided in this report, CTL Engineering should be notified so that our recommendations can be modified, if required. The proposal includes 38 sublots ranging between .75 acres and 1.48 acres on a public cul-desac street served by central water and sewer. This Preliminary Plan extension is identical to the original Preliminary Plan approved in November 2024. RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE WITH MODIFICATIONS ADJACENT ZONING/LAND USE Direction North East South West Zoning R-R Rural Residential R-R Rural Residential R-R Rural Residential R-1/PUD Rural Residential/Planned Unit Dev. Proposal: The applicant proposes the following on the 77.30-acre site: • Thirty-eight sublots with a centralized large lake located on the southern portions of six sublots; • One permanent public cul-de-sac on Street A; and • Two Open Space Blocks totaling 42+acres. Access: Access to the site is through one connection by Marks Road. Site Conditions: The parcel includes a residence and small lake on the western edge, a large lake in the central section, evergreen forest on the eastern edge, and cropland. Riparian areas are located on the southwestern edge leading to the centralized large lake and the southeastern edge of the parcel. Land Use Residence Residential Subdivision Cropland Residential Subdivisions Habermann Preliminary Plan Extension Brunswick Hills Comprehensive Plan: Adopted in May 2005, the Vision and Preferred Development Characteristics of the Comprehensive Plan were accepted by consensus. • • • • • Well-planned and enforced development that implements the will of the community. Attractive and useful open spaces that link the community. Public water service available to all residents. A Rural Visual character dominated by natural open spaces. A diverse and fiscally strong economic base that supports the health of the entire community. Brunswick Hills Zoning: The parcel is zoned R-R Rural Residential. The Brunswick Hills Township Zoning Resolution (ZR) Article IV Section 402 indicates the following. This district is established to provide for detached single-family dwellings on large lots with very low densities in a semi-rural atmosphere in locations consistent with and in furtherance of the vision and recommendations contained in the Comprehensive Land Use Plan in order to preserve the established character and nature of the Township. It is the further intent of this district to preserve significant areas of open space, retain rural vistas, and limit the density of development consistent with the rural nature of the Township and its public facilities, services, and infrastructure. The subdivision plans to apply for the Conservation Development Overlay District outlined in the ZR Article IV Section 411. These Conservation Development Overlay District regulations are established in accordance with the provisions of Section 519.021 of the Ohio Revised Code. In accordance with the provisions and standards contained herein, a Conservation Development Overlay District may be established in areas classified as R-R Rural Residential District on the Zoning Districts Map. Until such time as a property owner applies for and receives approval for a Conservation Development Overlay District as provided herein, the underlying provisions of the R-R Rural Residential District shall apply to the property. Upon approval of a Conservation Development Overlay District, the R-R Rural Residential District regulations shall no longer be applicable to the property so designated and the standards and requirements of this Section shall apply to and control development and use of all properties within said District. The primary objective of the Conservation Development Overlay District is to promote the health and safety of the community through the application of flexible land development techniques in the arrangement and construction of dwelling units and roads. Such flexibility is intended to: A. Maximize the permanent preservation and conservation of open space; B. Permit creative and imaginative layouts which respect environmental features; C. Maintain the one dwelling unit per two acre density of the Township’s more rural areas; D. Maximize protection of sensitive natural resource areas; E. Reduce the quantity and improve the quality of storm water runoff from expected development; Dept. of Planning Services Page 2 of 5 November 4, 2026 Habermann Preliminary Plan Extension F. Maintain natural features and characteristics (such as woods, hedgerows, natural vegetation, meadows, slopes and streams); G. Reduce the amount of disturbed land, the conversion of natural areas to landscaped areas for lawns, and the use of invasive vegetation; and H. Maintain the rural character of the Township. The soils that make up the majority of the build site are Mahoning silt loam with 0-2% slopes and 2-6% slopes (MgA and MgB) and Ellsworth silt loam with 2-6% and 6-12% Dept. of Planning Services Page 3 of 5 November 4, 2026 Habermann Preliminary Plan Extension slopes (ElB and ElC2). Slow permeability, seasonal wetness and seasonal high water table are limitations for these soils. 2. Wetland inventory maps indicate wetland classifications for the two existing ponds on the property. Any activity impacting wetlands is regulated by the US Army Corps of Engineers and/or Ohio EPA. 3. Stormwater management and sediment control practices should be implemented to mitigate the effects for excess runoff into water bodies. This could be silt fence or straw tubes in drainage areas. 4. Ensure that all setbacks are maintained in regards to the stormwater management basins and drainage easement. Maintain stormwater management basins throughout all stages of construction. 5. We recommend a plan for maintenance and operation be in place for the responsible party(s) in maintaining the stormwater management basins. This plan could include an updated and reinforced spillway design, removal of debris, invasive plants, and sediment build-up. 6. Brunswick Hills Township has a Riparian Setback extending from the southwest portion of the existing pond/stormwater management basin to the west-southwest toward Marks Road as well as in the far southeast corner. The southeast wooded portion that contains the Riparian Setback should be left as open space. Avoid disturbing or building within these setbacks. 7. Approximately 23 acres of watershed drain into the existing pond/stormwater basin and approximately 45 acres to the proposed stormwater management basin at the northwest corner of the subdivision. Ensure basins are designed to handle the capacity of runoff during large rain events. 8. Drainage across this property must maintain its natural flow path, as it did prior to any grading or construction activities on this site. Refer to Ohio Drainage Law. 9. The owners of sub-lots 24-32 must observe the limitations set forth with owning a section of the stormwater easement. 10. Our office would like to suggest green infrastructure considerations such as curb cuts, vegetative swales, and pervious surfaces. These practices help with storm water filtration, lessen flooding potential, and reduce erosion damages for downstream communities. 11. Tree removal should be limited to the construction site only. 12. Portions of this property had been formerly cropland and likely has field tile across it. Medina County Tax Map Office: CONDITIONAL APPROVAL taxmaps@medinaco.org 330.725.9777 Habermann Subdivision and Bridle Path Lane have been added to the reserved subdivision and road name lists. The surveyor has sent in a preliminary review of the final plat, and the tax map office has provided comments to the surveyor. Staff Comments: 1. The Final Plat was approved with modifications by the Planning Commission in August 2026 but has not been recorded. This extension is required because the Preliminary Plan expires on November 6, 2026. 2. The following data/information was not provided on or with the Preliminary Plan submittal Dept. of Planning Services Page 4 of 5 November 4, 2026 Habermann Preliminary Plan Extension as outlined in Article IV Section 404(C) of the Subdivision Regulations: a. (2)c.9. The enabling declaration; the declaration of covenants, conditions and restrictions, the articles of incorporation; and the corporate by-laws. b. (2)c.18. Wetlands –The developer shall contact in writing the applicable U.S. Army Corp of Engineers (USACE) District Office regarding the proposed subdivision and shall submit such correspondence to the Medina County Planning Commission as a condition of Preliminary Plan approval. Staff Comment: At the November 2024 Planning Commission meeting, the Preliminary Plan was approved with modifications. At that time, the applicant indicated the wetlands were approved by the USACE and they were waiting for the final letter. Staff recommend the applicant submit the correspondence from the USACE. c. (2)d.4. All related watershed boundaries, indicating in which watershed the subdivision is located, and all known underground drainage tile systems. This may be presented as a map insert on the same page. d. (2)d.7. A copy of the Developers Notice of Intent to obtain an Ohio E.P.A. stormwater management permit if applicable. 3. (4)b.1. The Preliminary Plan meets the standards and requirements of the Subdivision Regulations and conforms to the Township Zoning Resolution. The Township indicated the Preliminary Plan is conditionally approved. 4. (4)b.2. The Medina County Sanitary Engineer has determined the subdivision will be adequately serviced by central water and sanitary sewer subject to approval of detailed plans. 5. (4)b.3. The Medina County Engineer has determined the Preliminary Plan for streets, stormwater management and natural drainage ways protection are acceptable subsequent to the approval of more detailed construction drawings. Recommendation: The Department of Planning Services Staff recommend that the Medina County Planning Commission Approve with Modifications the Habermann Preliminary Plan Extension pending submission of the required data/information and satisfying all regulatory agency comments of previous and current staff reports. text: Preliminary Plan & Final Plat Sainato Estates Granger Township Meeting: App. No.: Applicant: Engineer: Parcels: Site Area: November 4, 2026 086-2026 PP FP David Sainato Rolling & Hocevar, Inc. 005-07C-30-005 30.2474 acres Sublots: Zoning: Utilities: School: Reviewer: 3 Sublots R-1 Residential District and C-1 Commercial District On-site Septic and Central Water Highland Local Alexander Zavertnik EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The 30.2474-acre site is located west of Ridge Road (SR 94) and south of Granger Road including two zoning districts. The applicant proposes three sublots ranging between 5.7890 and 13.46 acres, 4.36 acres of open space, and one private street leading to a permanent culde-sac. The Preliminary Plan expired in July 2024 requiring the applicant to restart the timeline. The Planning Commission Approved with Modifications a Final Plat in March of 2025. The Planning Commission will need to vote on the Preliminary Plan and Final Plat separately. PREMININARY PLAN RECOMMENDATION: APPROVAL FINAL PLAT RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE WITH MODIFICATIONS ADJACENT ZONING/LAND USE Direction North East South West Zoning R-1 Rural Residential/ C-1 Commercial R-1 Rural Residential/ C-1 Commercial R-1 Rural Residential/ C-1 Commercial R-1 Rural Residential Proposal: The applicant proposes three sublots for single-family homes with 4.50 acres of open space to be served by a private street. The Preliminary Plan proposes four stormwater basins with water quality abilities that will treat the stormwater runoff from the private street. One in Sublot 3 and the rest in Open Space Block “C”. Access: Access to the site is proposed at SR 94 leading to a private street that terminates in a permanent cul-de-sac. Site Conditions: Most of the planned site is deciduous forest including two existing wetlands. Land Use Residential/Deciduous Forest Ridge Road/Residential Residential/Deciduous Forest Cropland Sainato Estates Final Plat Granger Township Zoning Resolution: The western and majority portion of the site is zoned R-1 Rural Residential District, and the eastern portion of the site with access on SR 94 is zoned C-1 Commercial District. The purpose of the R-1 Residential District “is to manage low-density residential development that will preserve the rural residential character of Granger Township.” The minimum lot size is two acres and the minimum required frontage is 175 feet. The purpose of the C-1 Local Commercial District “is to provide for retail and service businesses serving the daily needs of Township residents for goods and services. C-1 Districts are strategically located to provide accessibility to Township residents. Uses in this district shall be compatible with surrounding residential uses in order to minimize impacts on surrounding neighborhoods and are intended to be limited in scale.” Agency Comments: Italicized text indicates agency comments. title: VALLEY RIDGE ESTATES, Preliminary Plan, 087-2026 PP, Liverpool Township
text: Preliminary Plan Valley Ridge Estates Liverpool Township Meeting: App. No.: Applicant: Engineer: Parcels: November 4, 2026 087-2026 PP Dave Kolar Davey Resource Group 025-01A-37-001 025-01A-43-002 025-01A-43-003 025-01A-43-038 025-01A-43-039 Site Area: Sublots: Zoning: 172.0 acres 143 Sublots R-R Rural Residential District with Controlled Density Overlay District (CDZ) Utilities: Central Sewer and Water School Dist.: Buckeye Local Reviewer: Denise Testa EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The 172-acre site is located northwest of downtown Valley City and north of Center Road (SR 303) including two points of access. The applicant proposes 143 sublots between 0.83 and 1.2 acres leading to two permanent cul-de-sacs. RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE WITH MODIFICAITONS ADJACENT ZONING/LAND USE Direction Zoning North R-R Rural Residential District East South West R-R Rural Residential District C-1 Commercial District R-R Rural Residential District R-R Rural Residential District Proposal: The applicant proposes 143 sublots for single-family homes with central sewer and water, 91+acres of open space in five blocks, and six stormwater retention ponds. Access: Access to the site is through two connections on Center Road (SR 303) leading to six public streets and five permanent cul-de-sacs. Site Conditions: Most of the planned site is used for agriculture in open fields. A stream and woodlands are located in the southeast portion and two wetlands in the central portion of the site. The site includes six abandoned oil or gas wells. Land Use Single-Family Residences Single-Family Residences Liverpool Township Offices Single-Family Residences Agriculture Single-Family Residence Valley Ridge Estates Preliminary Plan Liverpool Township Development Policy Plan: The proposed subdivision is consistent with the 2015 Liverpool Township Development Policy Plan’s Goal 2 which seeks to “promote the rural atmosphere of the Township while providing for balanced growth.” The site is designated for residential use on the Future Land Use Map, and the proposed subdivision conforms to this planned land use classification. Liverpool Township Zoning Resolution: According to the Liverpool Township Zoning Resolution (ZR), the purpose of R-R Rural Residential district is to provide for rural residential development at a low density which will promote the continuation of the predominant rural residential character of the Township. Where central sewer and water are available, it is the intention of this district to provide for low density residential development at a density of one (1) acre per dwelling unit. To ensure that existing and planned sewer and water facilities are most efficiently utilized, the one (1) acre per dwelling unit density will not be permitted outside the planned service areas as indicated in the Liverpool Township Development Policy Plan. The ZR indicates the purpose of the Controlled Density Zoning (CDZ) Overlay District is to, “...promote the preservation and protection of the rural atmosphere of the Township while providing for anticipated residential development. To accomplish that purpose, Controlled Density Zoning encourages the permanent preservation of relatively large tracts of land (consisting of, but not limited to, open natural areas, woodlands, greenway systems, wildlife habitats, flood plains, agricultural lands, wetlands, and waterways) of the Rural Residential District. These provisions and requirements are established as alternatives to a number of the residential lot requirements found elsewhere in the Resolution. Reductions permitted in these requirements are in exchange for the permanent preservation of open space and other natural features that can benefit not only the residents of the development but the general population of the Township.” Agency Comments: Italicized text indicates agency comments. Bryan Snyder: DISAPPROVAL Liverpool Township zoninginspector@liverpooltwp.org 330.483.3102 Recommended Action: Disapproval is based on the fact that the BZA has not conducted the Hearing for the Conditional Use CDZ, and is subject of their approval. The development plan will have to be in compliance with Liverpool Twp. Zoning Resolution. Applicant will need to go before the Zoning Board of Appeals as a CDZ is a Conditionally Approved use of the property. Also required will be a copy of the Covenants and Restrictions as well [as] a copy of the Homeowners Association documents delineating use and ownership of the open spaces which has been submitted. Dept. of Planning Services Page 2 of 7 November 4, 2026 Valley Ridge Estates Preliminary Plan Chris McDaniel Valley City/Liverpool Township Fire Inspector cmcdaniwl@valleycityfire.com 330.483.3811 1. All fire hydrants shall be required by local adapted code to have 5" Storz ADAPTER fittings on all hydrants. I know the county MCSE has been pushing back but having the adapter does not require the builder to change anything about the hydrants per there specks the adapters are removal able and not built in they are a thread x Storz fittings and will fit the Mueller brand hydrants the county requires. All hydrants must be spaced 300ft apart. 2. On the last plan review MCSE required a min. Of a 12" new water main be put in going from Station Rd. With new hydrants all the way down to Street D. The furthest road to the East. I do not see that on these prints. 3. All address numbers shall be 6" in height with a 3/4" stroke or width. 4. OFC Appendix D Section 107.2 Remoteness Where 2 fire apparatus access roads are required, they shall be placed a distance apart equal to not less than one half of the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the property or area to be served measured in a straight line between access points. The code and commentary book explains it like this. This concept is similar to the dealing with the remoteness of exits in Section 1007.1.1 of the OFC. One of the primary reasons for multiple access roads is to ensure that if one access road is blocked or otherwise unavailable, another will allow access by the fire department. Therefore when more than one access road is required, those roads shall be separated by enough distance to avoid a situation where both would be blocked or unavailable simply because they are to close together. The separation of the streets does not meet the OFC standards the roads are separated by .14 miles that's 732ft. Medina County Tax Map Office taxmaps@medinacounty.gov 330.725.9777 No changes. Dept. of Planning Services Page 3 of 7 November 4, 2026 Valley Ridge Estates Preliminary Plan Jared Feller Ohio Department of Transportation (ODOT) jared.feller@dot.ohio.gov 419.207.7058 This section of SR 303 is considered a rural Category 3 roadway. The recommended intersection spacing for this location is 1 mile, and the minimum spacing is ½ mile. The proposed west street (Street A) is approximately 0.5 miles from Station Road. The proposed east street (Street D) is approximately 0.33 miles from Lester Road. There is approximately 0.15 miles between the proposed subdivision streets along SR 303. Section 5.2 of ODOT’s State Highway Access Management Manual states that it is generally desirable to minimize the number of intersections to the extent possible while balancing the need for access. Existing reasonable access to the local street network should be considered prior to approving a new intersection on the State Highway System. The developer submitted a variance request for Street A and Street D along SR 303. ODOT District has reviewed the variance request and will permit full movement access at Street A and right-in/right-out only access at Street D. A traffic study has been completed for the development and showed that an eastbound left turn lane is warranted along SR 303 at Street A as shown on the Preliminary Plan. The property owner/developer will need to submit a permit application to ODOT District 3 for the approved access and left turn lane along SR 303. An ODOT permit will need to be issued before any work can be done within the SR 303 right-of-way. Ben Romine Medina County Sanitary Engineer’s Office bromine@medinacounty.gov 330.723.9575 The Medina County Sanitary Engineer (MCSE) has water and sanitary available to service this subdivision. For the sanitary sewer, the developer must extend sanitary sewer along the frontage of the subdivision to the westernmost property line. For all sanitary sewer easements, the width of the easement is to be twice the depth of the sewer. The MCSE’s existing water mains will need to be upgraded to service the proposed subdivision. These upgrades include the replacement of the 6” water main on Center Road (SR 303) with a 12” water main between Dallas Street & Street A or a 12” water main between Station Road and Street D. Detailed engineering plans at the time of construction must meet the current Code of Regulations for water and sanitary sewer per the MCSE. Dept. of Planning Services Page 4 of 7 November 4, 2026 Valley Ridge Estates Preliminary Plan Erik Malinoski: CONDITIONAL APPROVAL Medina County Engineer’s Office emalinoski@medinacounty.gov 330.764.8879 1. Drainage Maintenance Fund required. 2. Maintain existing watersheds. 3. Overland flood routes and rear yard drainage conveyance to be addressed with subdivision drawings. 4. Show mailbox kiosk locations. 5. Update notes in pavement section detail sheet. 6. Show existing pond outlets. Pond outlets to be evaluated for future use. 7. Sublots 119, 120 and 121 have portions of the existing pond located on them. Who will be responsible for maintenance of the pond? 8. Stormwater management easements to be clear of all trees and brush. 9. All utilities to be located a minimum of 5’ from edge of pavement. 10. Provide well plugging reports for all plugged wells on the parcels. 11. Vertical and horizontal road geometry should follow the standards in the Engineering Code for Subdivision Development. 12. It appears that there is extensive field tile located on these parcels. All field tile encountered during construction is to be tied into the proposed storm sewer system. 13. Show phase lines if this subdivision is being constructed in phases. Jim Smith Medina County Soil and Water Conservation District jsmith@medinacounty.gov 330.722.9317 Comments from the Concept Plan: 1. This site is made up of Ellsworth silt loam with 2-6% slopes (ElB) with limitations of seasonal wetness, a clayey subsoil, and slow permeability and 25-70% slopes (ElF) with limitations of primarily steep slopes. Mahoning silt loam with 0-2% slopes (MgA) with limitations of seasonal wetness, slow permeability, and a subsoil that is plastic when wet. Fitchville silt loam with 0-2% slopes (FcA) with limitations of seasonal wetness, soil material that is soft and compressible when wet, high potential frost action, and moderately slow permeability. title: WHITE OAK ESTATES (fka Rankin) Preliminary Plan and Variances, 077-2026 V-PP, Granger Township
text: Variance Request and Preliminary Plan White Oak Estates Granger Township Meeting: App. No.: Applicant: Engineer: Parcels: November 4, 2026 077-2026 V-PP Pulte Group, Inc. Cunningham & Assoc., Inc. 005-07B-16-028/032/033 005-07B-22-056 Site Area: Sublots: Zoning: Utilities: School: Reviewer: 100.46 acres 38 Sublots R-1 Residential District On-Site Septic and Private Wells Highland Local Denise Testa EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The 100+ acre site is located south of Interstate 271 (I-271), north of Remsen Road and west of State Road. The applicant proposes 38 sublots and one open space block on public streets leading to permanent public cul-de-sacs. The applicant has requested a variance to Section 604(B)(9) Street Stubs and Cul-de-sacs of the Medina County Subdivision Regulations (Regulations) which states that a permanent culde-sac street shall not exceed 2,500 feet in length. The Planning Commission will need to vote on each item separately. VARIANCE RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE PRELIMINARY PLAN RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE WITH MODIFICATIONS ADJACENT ZONING/LAND USE Direction North East South West Zoning R-1 Rural Residential R-1 Rural Residential R-1 Rural Residential R-1 Rural Residential Proposal: The applicant proposes the following to be completed in two phases: • 38 sublots ranging between 2 and 5+ acres for single-family homes; • 3+ acres of open space; • Two public streets leading to two permanent cul-de-sacs; • Two stormwater management basins with one also functioning as a fire pond; • 25-foot riparian setback for all undisturbed wetlands; and • Wetland impacts of 0.3540 acres. Land Use Residential/Deciduous Forest/I-271 Residential/State Road Residential/Deciduous Forest/Remsen Road Cropland/Residential White Oak Estates Variance and Preliminary Plan Access: Access to the site is proposed at State Road creating two public streets that lead to two permanent public cul-de-sacs. Site Conditions: The site has rolling topography, with elevations generally decreasing toward the drainage features located through the southern portion of the property. A mapped stream extends generally from west to east through the southern portion of the area shown on the aerial map. Areas of wooded vegetation and lower-lying ground are associated with this drainage corridor. The site includes abandoned gas wells on proposed Sublots 9, 13, 16, 23/24, 28, 31 and the Open Space Block. Sublot 25 includes a culvert. Several wetland and surface-water features are mapped within and adjacent to the subject property. These include wetland areas and ponds concentrated along the existing drainage corridor, as well as additional ponds and wetland features on adjacent properties. The aerial mapping also depicts wooded areas associated with portions of the drainage system. The subject property is located within the Rocky River drainage basin. The local drainage system includes Allard Creek, which flows to the East Branch Rocky River. In summary, the subject parcels consist of a combination of open agricultural land, wooded areas, rolling terrain, and areas associated with existing streams, drainage features, wetlands, and surface water. The location and extent of these existing physical features are depicted on the aerial and environmental maps included with this report. Granger Township Zoning Resolution The site is zoned R-1 Rural Residential District. According to the Granger Township Zoning Resolution (ZR), the purpose of the R-1 Residential District “…is to manage low-density residential development that will preserve the rural residential character of Granger Township.” The minimum lot size is two acres and the minimum required frontage is 175 feet. The ZR does not require riparian setbacks and does not include a conservation development option for the R-1 District. Staff recommend the applicant consult with the Township Zoning Inspector to ensure compliance with the ZR and confirm the applicable review/approval procedures. Dept. of Planning Services Page 2 of 8 November 4, 2026 White Oak Estates Variance and Preliminary Plan VARIANCE REQUEST 1. Variance Request The applicant has requested a variance from Section 604(B)(9), Street Stubs and Cul-de-sacs, of the Medina County Subdivision Regulations (Regulations), which limits the length of a permanent cul-de-sac street to 2,500 feet. The proposed length of Wojtowicz Way is 3,643 feet, representing an increase of approximately 46 percent over the maximum permitted length, while the proposed length of Cannata Way is 2,920 feet, representing an increase of approximately 17 percent. 2. Site Conditions and Access Considerations. The Granger Township Zoning Inspector has indicated that the Township prefers that access to the subdivision be provided solely from State Road. Although the property has frontage on Remsen Road, establishing an additional access point would require disturbance of the existing creek and could impact the rural character of the area. Staff note that the requested variance allows the subdivision to be designed in a manner that minimizes environmental impacts while accommodating the Township’s preferred access arrangement. 3. Variance Criteria Section 203(A)(2) of the Regulations establishes the criteria for granting variances. Staff comments regarding compliance with these criteria are provided below: a. The MCPC must find that an unnecessary hardship may result from the strict application of the Regulations due to exceptional topographic or other conditions. The combination of the site’s physical characteristics, the presence of the creek, and the Township’s preference for a single access point from State Road creates circumstances that limit roadway design options. Requiring strict compliance with the 2,500-foot standard would likely necessitate additional roadway connections or a significant redesign of the subdivision layout, resulting in greater environmental disturbance. The requested variances represent an approach that balances site constraints with the overall objectives of the Regulations. b. The MCPC may vary the Regulations to relieve an established hardship, provided such relief can be granted without detriment to the public interest and without impairing the intent and purpose of the Regulations or the desirable development of the neighborhood and community. The Regulations state that the cul-de-sac length limitation is intended to promote “greater convenience to traffic, more effective police and fire protection, and efficiency of road maintenance.” The Granger Fire Department has no concerns about the proposed street lengths on the permanent cul-de-sacs. Based on the information submitted, the proposed street lengths do not appear to adversely affect internal traffic circulation or roadway maintenance. Granting the variance would not appear to impair the intent and purpose of the Regulations or the desirable development of the subdivision and surrounding area. Dept. of Planning Services Page 3 of 8 November 4, 2026 White Oak Estates Variance and Preliminary Plan c. The Regulations provide criteria for determining hardship and granting relief but do not establish specific standards regarding the amount of a variance that may be approved. Over the past 19 years, the MCPC has granted five variances related to cul-de-sac length, with approved increases ranging from approximately 5.6 percent to 37.6 percent above the permitted maximum. The average increase granted was approximately 17.7 percent. The requested variance for Cannata Way is generally consistent with prior approvals, while the requested variance for Wojtowicz Way exceeds the range of past approvals and has been evaluated in the context of the site constraints, environmental considerations, Township access preferences, and comments received from emergency service providers. Recommendation: For further consideration, the applicant has included additional materials in the attached Variance Summary & Exhibits including maps highlighting cul-de-sac street lengths of other Granger Township subdivisions. The Department of Planning Services staff recommend the Planning Commission to Approve both variances for the White Oak Estates Preliminary Plan. Angela Fritz TC Energy/US Crossings Us_crossings@tcenergy.com 800-562-8931 Per our land representative, TC Energy is not impacted by the “White Oak Estates (FKA Rankin) Preliminary Plan &Variance Request.” Medina County Soil and Water Conservation District jsmith@medinacounty.org 330.722.9317 Comments from the Concept Plan: 1. Majority of this project site is made up of Ellsworth silt loam with greater than 2-6% slopes and 6-12% slopes. Restrictions with these soil types are slope, seasonal wetness, slow permeability, a clayey subsoil. Areas of ElC2 soils are classified as moderately erodible. 2. Sublots 10-14, 32 and 33 have wetlands within their boundaries that are planned to be filled. US Army Corps of Engineers and/or Ohio EPA should be involved with plans for impacting wetlands. 3. Stormwater management basins should have a plan that outlines the party responsible for maintenance and monitoring of the dam/spillway of the basin(s). 4. Fire ponds should be approved by the respective township zoning inspector and local fire department. 5. Wetlands on site that are not planned to be impacted should have the riparian setbacks observed and followed throughout all phases of construction. 6. In areas where there’s land disturbance on slopes greater than 6%, it is encouraged to utilize excessive sediment and erosion control practices until the ground has vegetative establishment. 7. Watershed and natural drainage paths should be maintained throughout all phases of construction. 8. It is recommended that tree removal stay limited to the immediate construction area only. It is encouraged to leave healthy trees standing near wetland areas to preserve the soil structure and natural features of the wetlands. This increases stormwater holding capacity, improves water quality, and reduces future risk of erosion. 9. This property had been in agriculture use and may have subsurface drain tile throughout the property. It is recommended to locate and address existing tile accordingly. Staff recommend the applicant contact Planning Services if the Preliminary Plan requires significant revisions during the construction and improvement phase to determine if Planning Commission review is required. 2. Staff recommend the applicant adjust these sublot lines to avoid any confusion. 3. The Article II Section 2.1(C) of the Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Easements and Restrictions indicate that fire hydrant is defined as one of the “Areas of Responsibility.” Staff recommend revising “fire hydrant” to “dry hydrant and fire pond” because fire hydrants are not located in this subdivision. Members shall conduct themselves in a professional manner. Updated 11/4/2026 at 2:14 PM 2 Fall Planning Meeting 2026 November 5, 2026 Fire Department Items - Exhibit A Deputy Fire Marshal With the recent approval of the Norwich Township Permit and Fee Schedule, I would like to promote a Deputy Fire Marshal in the ﬁre prevention bureau. This position would oversee all plan review, Community Risk Reduction eﬀorts, and Focus Hilliard. No additional hiring will need to take place to ﬁll this position. EMS Needs from fund 2281 Pediatric Cot Restraint System- $19,440 – The simplest and most eﬀective way to properly secure a child from 4-108 pounds. Can also put on top of a parent and secure a 4–22-pound child. Compatible with our current power cots. Radios-$42,000 – We still have 22 APX7000 radios that are end-of-life. Sixteen of these are on front line apparatus. We are currently losing 3-4 radios a year that cannot be ﬁxed. This request and a similar amount in 2028 will replace all the end-of-life walkies. Radios replaced with new walkies are moved to “spare” to backﬁll OOS radios and will eventually be used as training radios in “The Den.” Ultra Sound-$12,000-Purchase two ultra sound machines to be placed in service in the EMS supervisor’s vehicle. The plan is to add two additional in 2028 to be placed on all frontline medics. Medic Re-Chassis-Moving the patient care area from an old EMS transport vehicle to a new vehicle. A re-chassis takes less than one year to complete. The total cost of this project is $300,000. In comparison, a new EMS transport vehicle now exceeds $400,000 with a two-year delivery time. OperationsAirpack-$205,000 Our current MSA self-contained breathing apparatus are at the end of life. In 2026 we replaced 20 of our air packs. The purchase of an additional 20 will completely update our ﬂeet. Moving forward, we will replace air packs when we replace apparatus in an eﬀort to keep costs low. 1 Utility Truck-Replacing Utility 83 with a larger F350 crew cab pick up truck. The total cost to complete this project is $82,000. The current Utility truck is at it’s max limit with pulling power when pulling our Decon Trailer. The new truck allows the entire crew to respond in the same vehicle for Hazmat responses. Turnout Gear-Replacement turnout gear for old and expiring sets currently in circulation. This is part of our established replacement cycle and the total cost is $30,000. NRECC Capital Expenses-The CAD system (Computer Aided Dispatching) for our alarm oﬃce is becoming obsolete soon. The contract with NRECC requires that all partner agencies share the expense of major Capital purchases. Our portion to purchase a new CAD System in 2027 is $250,000. This is in addition to our normal dispatching fees. Building Needs Station Alerting-Upgrading the station alerting at Station 83 would allow our members to get to our apparatus timelier. By adding dorm remotes and indicator lights throughout the building, our members become more eﬃcient and better rested. The total cost of this project will be $47,000. Bay Lighting-Upgrading the bay lighting at Station 83 from traditional halogen bulbs to LED bulbs and new ﬁxtures. The current lighting is original to the building and has a dark and cavernous feel. The total cost of this project will be $7,000. Shower Replacement-We have repeatedly repaired the showers in the men’s restroom at Station 81 adding foam and sand to the ﬂoor below the showers. This ﬁx is temporary and the long-term solution is to completely remove the showers, repair the ﬂoor, and replace the showers. The total cost of this project will be $61,000. Painting-Interior painting at station 81 totaling $45,000. This includes all interior spaces on the ﬁre side of the building including the apparatus bay. LED Strip Lighting-Adding LED lighting along the overhead bay doors to indicate if the bay door is open completely or not. The total cost to do this project at Station’s 81 and 83 is $25,000. 2

text: Changes to the Brown Township Zoning Resolution Article 4 – Definitions Section 4.01: Borrow Pit (General): A pit adjacent to a fill or embankment from which material is taken for the purpose of making the fill or constructing and maintaining that embankment. A temporary excavation from which soil, sand, gravel, clay, or similar earthen materials are removed solely for use in connection with a specific construction or public improvement project, and not for commercial sale to the general public. Borrow Pit (Off-Site): A temporary excavation located on a parcel separate from the parcel(s) on which the construction or public improvement project utilizing the excavated materials is located. Borrow Pit (On-Site): A temporary excavation located on the same parcel or contiguous parcels under common ownership as the construction or public improvement project for which the excavated materials are used. Data Center: A building, structure, or group of buildings or structures primarily used to house computer servers, data storage systems, networking equipment, or other computing equipment for the storage, management, processing, transmission, or exchange of digital data. The term includes facilities used for cryptocurrency mining, blockchain processing, or other high-density computational activities. A Data Center may include accessory infrastructure and equipment necessary for its operation, including electrical substations, transformers, switchgear, uninterruptible power supply systems, battery energy storage systems, backup generators, cooling and heat-rejection systems, water treatment or storage systems, telecommunications equipment, and security facilities. A Data Center does not include an office, corporate headquarters, telecommunications switching facility, or other establishment in which data processing or storage is incidental or subordinate to the principal use. Net Developable Area/Acreage: The net area left after deducting from a planned unit development tract’s gross acreage: The Area/Acreage remaining from a planned unit development tract’s gross acreage after deducting: 1.) Right of way for streets and utilities (15% of gross acreage when estimating density); 2.) Jurisdictional wetlands, as defined US Army Corps of Engineers’ Corps of Engineers Wetlands Delineation Manual, Technical Report Y-87-1, U.S. Army Engineer Waterways Experiment Station, Vicksburg, Miss. Jurisdictional wetlands as regulated by Section 404 of the Clean Water Act consist of : a) Hydric soils, b) Hydrophytic vegetation and c) Wetland hydrology (this generally means they support more than 50% wetland vegetation, and are poorly drained soils which are periodically inundated or saturated ); 3.) Floodplains within a FEMA 100-year floodplain; 4.) Slopes greater than 20%, including ravines shown to be critical resource areas on the Brown Township Comprehensive Plan; 5.) Utility rights-of-way and easements for above-ground and currently existing utility structures such as above ground pipelines and existing overhead electric transmission (not 6.) Local service) wires; 7.) Existing bodies of water. Tract: An area, parcel, site, piece of land, or property that is the subject of a development application. Any lot or group of lots which are contiguous or adjacent to one another that are intended and proposed to be constructed as a singular planned development, regardless of whether construction of said development occurs in phases. All concepts and definitions pertaining to lots, such as frontage, lot lines, setback, and yard, shall apply to tracts. Article 5 – Districts and Boundaries Section 5.01: For the purpose of this Resolution, the following districts are hereby created in order that the unincorporated area of Brown Township, Delaware County, Ohio, may be divided into one or more such districts: FR-1 – Farm Residence District R-2 – Low Density Residential District R-3 – Medium Density Residential District PRD – Planned Residence District C-2 – Neighborhood Commercial District PC – Planned Commercial and Office District PI – Planned Industrial District A-1 – Agricultural Preservation District PUD – Planned Unit Development PFRCD – Planned Farm Residential Conservation District Commented [BZ1]: Changed Section 5.052 – Low Density Residential District (R-2): The R-2 district is provided for sections of the township with moderately low-density single family residential development, and access to centralized water and sewer systems. Minimum lot size is 29,600 8,700 square feet. Section 5.053 – Medium Density Residential District (R-3): Commented [BZ2]: Changed to follow the updates made to the R-2 District The R-3 district is provided in appropriate areas of the township for single family dwellings, and conditionally, multifamily residential development where there is access to centralized water and sewer systems, and a land access to a major collector or arterial street. Section 5.057 – Neighborhood Commercial District (C-2) The Neighborhood Commercial district was intended to encourage groupings of small retail establishments to promote convenient shopping to residential neighborhoods in the time before the township adopted Planned Commercial zoning. The Neighborhood Commercial District is now archaic and is retained only for the benefit of land already so zoned. It is a standard district, not a Planned Unit Development. Commented [BZ3]: The R-3 Zoning District will be removed Commented [BZ4]: Article on C-2 was deleted previously Section 5.0563 – Agricultural Conservation District (A-1) The Agricultural Conservation District is provided for landowners that wish to voluntarily place their land in an exclusively agricultural zoning district. Article 6 – Farm Residence District (FR-1) Section 6.03 : Sections 519.02 to 519.25 of the Ohio Revised Code confer power on a board of township trustees or board of zoning appeals with respect to the location, erection, construction, reconstruction, change, alteration, removal or enlargement of a telecommunications tower, but not with respect to the maintenance or use of such tower or any change or alteration that would not substantially increase the tower’s height. Public utilities or other functionally equivalent providers may site a telecommunications tower as a Conditional Use in zoning districts FR-1, R-2, R-3, PRD or Owner Initiated Planned Unit Development, provided that the following conditions are met (in addition to any other applicable criteria): Section 6.04 : As used in this section, “small wind farm” means wind turbines and associated facilities in a single interconnection to the electrical grid and designed for, or capable of, operation at an aggregate capacity of less than five megawatts. Wind Projects Farms of 6MW or more shall be required to submit an application with the Ohio Power Siting Board (OPSB) at the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (PUCO) and are required to meet OPSB regulations. Small Wind Projects Farms less than 5MW and used solely for Agriculture will be exempt from these zoning regulations as an Agricultural Use. Any proposed construction, erection, or siting of a small wind project farm less than 5MW including the wind turbine generator or anemometer or any parts thereof shall be a Permitted Use/Permit Required in any zoning district except those expressly zoned for residential use. A Conditional Use Permit shall be required in all districts zoned for residential use. The areas zoned for residential use shall be deemed to be all land located within the following Commented [BZ5]: Removing this District from the Resolution districts: Farm Residential (FR-I), Planned Residential (PRD) and Planned Farm Residential Conservation District (PFRCD). Article 7 – Farm Residence District (FR-1) Section 7.02 – B: Accessory buildings and accessory, structures and uses including private garages and permanent dwellings for full time domestic help employed on the premises or full time farm labor. Section 7.02 – D: Temporary structures such as mobile or manufactured homes for temporary residential use and temporary structures of a nonresidential, including shipping containers, character may be used incident to construction work on the premises or on adjacent public projects or during a period while the permanent dwelling is being constructed. The user of said structure shall obtain a permit for such temporary use, which permit shall be valid for six (6) months and may be renewed not more than twice. Renewal of the permit shall be at the discretion of the Zoning Inspector on finding of reasonable progress toward completion of the permanent structure or project. The Zoning Inspector may require provisions for sanitary waste disposal, solid waste disposal and water supply, as he deems necessary. The fees for such permit and renewals thereof shall be established by the Board of Township Trustees. Said temporary structure shall be removed not later than ten (10) days after expiration of said permit. Section 7.02 – M: On-Site Borrow Pits: Provided that all requirements outlined in Section 21.18 of this Resolution are met Section 7.03 – Q: Off-Site Borrow Pits: Provided that all requirements outlined in Section 21.18 of this Resolution are met Section 7.05 – G: Rear Yard Requirement: No principal dwelling shall be located closer than eighty (80) feet to the rear line of any lot and no accessory building, structure or use, with the exception of fencing, shall be located closer than fifteen (15) feet to said rear lot line. Article 8 – Low Density Residential District (R-2) Section 8.02 – B: Accessory buildings and accessory, structures and uses including private garages. Section 8.05 – A: Lot Area: Residential lots which are served with approved central water and sewer systems serving all lots may be developed for such use if they have a lot area of not less than 29,600 8,700 square feet. All other parcels, not so serviced, shall contain the lot areas prescribed by the provisions of Article 7 of this Resolution. Commented [BZ6]: Clean up Section 8.05 – B: Lot Frontage: All lots or parcels developed within this district having an area of less than one (1) acre shall have a minimum lot frontage of one hundred (100) fifty (50) feet. All other lots or parcels shall have the minimum lot width of Seventy-five (75) feet on an adjoining approved street or road or approved CAD. Section 8.05 – G: Rear Yard Requirement: No principal dwelling shall be located closer than sixty-five (65) fifty (50) feet to the rear line of any lot and no accessory building, structure or use, with the exception of fencing, shall be located closer than fifteen (15) five (5) feet to said rear lot line. Article 9– Medium Density Residential District (R-3) Remove District Article 10 – Planned Residential District Section 10.03: The permitted density is the number of dwelling units in the development. Such number shall be determined by dividing the net developable area by the conventional lot size for the zoning district being overlaid. If the proposed open space development is located in more than one zoning district, then the total number of dwelling units allowed within the tract shall be the sum of those allowed for the portion of land lying within each zoning district. The permitted density shall be determined by dividing the number of proposed Dwelling Units by the Net Developable Acreage. Section 10.04: Planned Residential Development zoning may be overlaid on the FR-1 and the R-2 zones zoning district pursuant to a zoning map amendment approved by the township. The Brown Township Comprehensive Plan identifies the Planning Areas in which Planned Residential Developments (PRDs) are considered appropriate Section 10.05 – A: Single Family detached residential dwelling units in FR-1 and R2 PRD’s; single family attached dwellings (condominiums separated by vertical firewalls) in R-2 PRD’s. Commented [BZ7]: Changed Single Family detached residential dwelling units without Conservation Standards; Single Family attached dwellings (condominiums separated by vertical firewalls) with Conservation Standards Section 10.05 – B: Common Area Open Space - upon approval of the final development plan by the township, the following uses and improvements may be permitted in the common area: Section 10.05 – M: On-Site Borrow Pits: Provided that all requirements outlined in Section 21.18 of this Resolution are met Section 10.09 – A: All land within a proposed Planned Development shall be Contiguous and shall not be divided into parts by any state or federal limited access highway or by any railroad Right-of-Way. Section 10.09 – B: Unless otherwise permitted via a Divergence that has been reviewed and approved, the Density of land use within a Planned Residential District shall not exceed 1.0 Dwellings per Net Developable Acre when Conservation Development Standards are not utilized or 1.25 Dwellings per Net Developable Acre when Conservation Development Standards are utilized. Section 10.09 – D: No building shall be constructed within 50 feet of the perimeter property line of the overall PRD tract; Open Space areas shall be provided around the entire perimeter of a Tract. Such areas shall count towards the Planned Development’s required Open Space acreage. 1) The required widths of said area shall be: a) Fifty (50) feet from any Lot within a Planned Residential Zoning District. b) One hundred (100) feet from any Lot located within a Residential or Non-Residential Zoning District. c) One hundred (100) feet from the Right-of-Way line of any Street that is not classified as an Arterial or Collector Street. d) One hundred seventy (170) feet from the Right-of-Way line of any Arterial or Collector Street. 2) The perimeter of said area shall be planted with two (2) evergreen trees and three (3) deciduous trees for every fifty (50) feet of site perimeter. a) Required plantings shall be planted in staggered rows or groupings to create a natural looking landscape buffer but shall still generally cover the entire linear perimeter of the Tract. b) Required plantings shall adhere to the size requirements found in Article 23. c) In sections where existing woody vegetation, which is healthy, mature, and abundant enough to serve as a visual screen, occurs along the perimeter of the Tract, said vegetation may be credited towards the above planting requirements. 3) No Building or Structure shall be permitted within said area unless approved as part of the Planned Development’s Common Open Space 4) No Limited Common Element Area shall be permitted within said area Section 10.09 – I: Minimum overall tract size for a PRD is 40 25 acres, unless adjacent to a neighborhood of comparable density or design, in which case the Zoning Commission may permit the tract size to be reduced to 10 acres; Section 10.09 – M: The required percent of open space shall be provided. The percent of open space required varies according to the zoning district overlaid; FR-1- 40% (of gross tract area) open space R-2: - 20% (of gross tract area) open space Without Conservation Development Standards: 40% of the gross acreage of the tract will be Open Space, with a minimum of 15% being Common Open Space (accessible to the tenants or residents) With Conservation Development Standards: 50% of the gross acreage of the tract will be Open Space, with a minimum of 25% being Common Open Space (accessible to the tenants or residents) In calculating open space, the areas of fee simple lots conveyed to homeowners shall not be included. Unbuildable areas, as provided in Net Developable area calculation, may count for up to 50% of the required open space. That portion of land dedicated to public purposes that remain either open and unbuilt upon by any structure (including parking) or which houses a recreational facility approved by the Zoning Commission on the Development Plan may count toward the open space requirement. Section 10.09 – O: In FR-1 zones, water supply and sanitary sewage disposal shall be as approved by the Delaware County Board Health District and/or the Ohio EPA. Feasibility shall be indicated by the appropriate agency at the time of the preliminary plan. In the R-2 zone, centralized water supply and sanitary sewage disposal systems shall be provided, subject to Delaware County Sanitary Engineer, Health District and Ohio Environmental Protection Agency approval. Feasibility of water supply and wastewater disposal systems shall be indicated by the appropriate agencies at the time of the preliminary plan. Planned Residential Districts will only be allowed in areas served by central sanitary sewers and Central Water Systems, or developments utilizing other sewage treatment options approved in the development plan. The foregoing shall not preclude any property not meeting this standard but already within this District from being developed in accordance with the terms of this Zoning Resolution. Section 10.09 – R: Sidewalks or paths shall be provided in the area. Sidewalks shall be at least five feet (5’) wide and shall be separated from the paved street surface by at least five feet (5') six feet (6') of landscaped or grassed green strip. text: Section 21.14 – LIGHTING The intent and purpose of these standards is to reasonably regulate lighting in a manner which reduces or prevents light pollution and minimizes lighting impacts on surrounding lots. Except for lighting required or permitted by law and subject to public agency enforcement, lighting in AR-1 Agricultural Residential, and lighting in FR-1 Farm Residential districts, all exterior lighting shall comply with these standards unless specifically exempted or otherwise stipulated and/or modified by the regulations within a specific Zoning District of this Zoning Resolution. Lighting that existed prior to the effective date of this Resolution shall be considered a legal nonconforming use and may remain until the light fixture or supporting pole is replaced. Replacement lighting shall comply with this Article. A. Lighting Standards: 1. All outdoor lighting fixtures shall be full cutoff lighting fixtures as defined by this Resolution. 2. No lighting may be installed within a public right-of-way except where authorized or installed by government entities or their designees. 3. All lighting shall be directed downward and fully shielded to prevent direct visibility of the light source from adjoining properties and so as to not shine onto a roadway where it causes visibility interference to any driver or pedestrian. 4. Lighting poles or building mounted light fixtures shall not exceed a height of twelve (12) feet on parcels zoned for residential use and twenty (20) feet on parcels zoned for non-residential use. The height shall be measured from established finished grade adjacent to the light to the topmost point of the fixture. 5. All lighting must have a color temperature of 3,000 kelvin or less and must use light colors no bluer than “warm white”. 6. No lighting shall produce more than 1,600 lumens on parcels zoned for residential use and 3,000 lumens on parcels zoned for non-residential use. 7. Outdoor lighting fixtures on parcels zoned for non-residential uses must remain off between the hours of 10:00PM and 6:00AM. Lights used exclusively for safety and/or security purposes may remain on outside the prohibited hours, provided the lighting produces no more than 1,500 lumens. Automatic shut-off fixtures, auto dimming to adjust lighting 8. based on ambient lighting, and the use of as little lighting as necessary without creating safety issues are encouraged. Lighting shall be designed and located in accordance with the illumination levels outlined in the following table “Maximum Illumination Level at the Property Line”. Maximum illumination shall be measured in accordance with Section D below. Maximum Illumination Level at the Property Line Neighboring Property Zoning Maximum Illumination at the Classification Property Line All residential zoning districts 0.2 foot-candle All non-residential zoning districts 1.0 foot-candle B. Prohibited Lighting: 1. Search lights, beacons, digital lighting, laser source lights, rotating lights, flashing lights, blinking lights, fluttering lights, or any similar highintensity lights. 2. Uplighting, except for decorative lighting that is directed entirely at a building or used in a fountain and complies with all other aspects of this article. C. Exemptions to Prohibited Lighting: 1. Illuminated flagpoles for governmental or institutional flags when the flag is flying. 2. Temporary holiday lighting in use for 60 days or less. 3. Any outdoor lighting produced directly by fossil-fuel combustion. D. Light Measurement Technique: Light levels shall be measured at the lot line separating the subject property from any neighboring property. If measurement on private property is not possible or practical, light levels may be measured at the boundary of the public street right-of-way that adjoins the subject property or at any other location on the subject property. Measurements shall be made at finished grade (ground level), with the light-registering portion of the meter held parallel to the ground pointing up. Measurements shall be taken using a calibrated light meter capable of measuring horizontal foot-candles. ARTICLE IV – DEFINITION OF TERMS (to be added to Article IV. I have multiple options in some instances where we need to review and decide on which definition we want to use.) COLOR TEMPERATURE/ CORRELATED COLOR TEMPERATURE (CCT): A measure of light source color appearance, expressed in kelvins (K), ranging from one thousand degrees kelvin (1,000°K) to ten thousand degrees kelvin (10,000°K). FOOT-CANDLE: A unit that measures the amount of light that falls onto a surface as emitted by an exterior lighting device. For the purposes of this Resolution, foot-candle refers to horizontal foot-candles rather than vertical. FULLY SHIELDED (LIGHTING): A light fixture constructed in such a manner that all light emitted by the fixture, either directly from the lamp or a diffusing element, or indirectly by reflection or refraction from any part of the light fixture, is projected below the horizontal plane. LIGHT FIXTURE: A complete electrical device that holds a light bulb, has a power source, provides illumination, and is permanently or semi-permanently attached to a building, pole, structure, or other mounting source. UPLIGHTING: Any light source that is directed in such a manner as to shine light rays above the horizontal plane.

STAFF REPORT TO THE FAIRFIELD TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES MEETING DATE: NOVEMBER 10, 2026 CASE: FTZC26-3C APPLICANT: Butler County Engineer’s Office OWNER: Butler County Board of Commissioners LOCATION: 1921 Fairgrove Avenue A0300-026-000-108 CURRENTLY ZONED: R-MHP Residential Manufactured Home Park REQUEST: Zone change from R-MHP Residential Manufactured Home Park To B-2 General Business District SITUATION OF PROPERTY The subject property is located just on south side of Ohio State Route 4 (Fairgrove Avenue), east of North Fair Avenue, west of Campbell Drive at 1921 Fairgrove Avenue. The request applies to an approximately 0.875-acre portion of parcel A0300-026-000-108, located at 1955 Fairgrove Avenue and owned by the Butler County Board of Commissioners. The overall parcel contains approximately 4.24 acres. The submitted rezoning plat identifies the eastern approximately 0.875-acre portion as R-MHP Residential Manufactured Home Park District and the remainder as B-2 General Business District. The application identifies the existing use of the rezoning area as vacant land and an access drive serving the Butler County Engineer’s Office campus. Adjoining property to the east is zoned B-1 Neighborhood Business District. Property to the north, across Fairgrove Avenue and within the City of Hamilton, is zoned B-2 Community Business District. The adjoining properties to the west and south are associated with The Butler County Engineer’s Office campus. Property to the west is zoned B-2 General Business District, and to the south, within the City of Hamilton, is zoned Office Planned Unit Development (OPD). DESCRIPTION OF REQUEST The applicant is requesting a zone change of approximately 0.875 acres from R-MHP Residential Manufactured Home Park District to B-2 General Business District. The requested rezoning would allow this area to be incorporated into the planned campus expansion under the same zoning classification as the adjoining campus property to the west. The subject property consists of vacant land and an existing access drive serving the Butler County Engineer’s Office campus. The requested rezoning would allow this area to be incorporated into the planned campus expansion under the same zoning classification as the adjoining campus property to the west. FTZC26-3C | FINDINGS OF FACT The application identifies the current use of the rezoning area as vacant, land and an access drive serving the campus. The applicant states that the proposed access drive would remain near the existing drive and continue providing campus access. Based on the application documents, the existing facilities are insufficient to support the Operations Department’s snow and ice removal, bridge and roadway maintenance, culvert replacement, and mowing activities. The proposed campus expansion is intended to provide additional space, equipment accommodations, and infrastructure for these services. The floor plan identifies administrative offices, a conference room, employee support areas, heated vehicle storage, fabrication and service bays, equipment storage, and a vehicle wash bay. Proposed total building area is approximately 60,000 square feet and a building height of 34 feet. The plans illustrate the broader campus project and do not establish that the building would be located entirely within the rezoning area. The Fairfield Township Board of Zoning Appeals approved the three variances for building area, building height, and rear-yard setback associated with the broader campus expansion, These approvals are separate from the zoning map amendment before the Board of Trustees. Approved Variances The Board of Zoning Appeals approved the following dimensional variances: 1. A variance from Section 621.4(a) to permit a ground-floor building area of approximately 60,000 square feet, exceeding the maximum permitted 50,000 square feet. 2. A variance from Section 621.6 to permit a building height of 34 feet, exceeding the maximum permitted height of 30 feet. 3. A variance from Section 621.7 to permit a rear-yard setback of 10 feet, where a minimum of 25 feet is required. Relevant Sections of the Fairfield Township Zoning Resolution: 621, B-2 GENERAL BUSINESS DISTRICT PURPOSE. The intent of the B-2 General Business District is to reserve certain land areas for central commercial uses which serve the general and service needs of the residents of the Township. Their locations shall accommodate the most intensive commercial and office development and shall reflect areas of sound organized development. On October 21, 2026, the Fairfield Township Zoning Commission recommended approval to the Board of Trustees of the requested zone change for the approximately 0.875-acre portion of parcel A0300-026-000- 108 from R-MHP Residential Manufactured Home Park District to B-2 General Business District. The requested rezoning is now before the Board of Trustees for consideration. STAFF ANALYSIS Compatibility with Surrounding Zoning and Land Uses The requested zone change would extend the existing B-2 General Business District classification across the remaining R-MHP portion of the property. The rezoning area already provides access to the Butler County Engineer’s Office campus, and the request would support its continued use as part of that campus. The surrounding area includes business zoning and existing governmental facilities. The requested B-2 classification is compatible with this setting and would provide consistent zoning across the Township portion of the property. Consistency with the Comprehensive Plan The proposed B-2 General Business District is similar in its permitted uses to the Planned Business designation shown on the Comprehensive Plan’s Future Land Use Map. The requested rezoning would extend existing business zoning and support expansion of an established public service facility. The Comprehensive Plan encourages consideration of surrounding land uses, traffic safety, shared access and parking, and coordinated landscaping and lighting. The proposed integration of the rezoning area into the existing campus is generally consistent with these planning principles.
