NEW BUSINESS Case No. ZON-26-11 — 7328 - 7348 Hayden Run Road, Brown Township Applicant/Owner: Property owner, represented by Jack Reynolds, Esq., Smith and Hale. Request: Rezoning of 3.57 acres from the Rural district to the Select Commercial Planned District (SCPD) for a personal self-storage complex with office use. Staff Presentation Mr. Workman presented the staff report, summarizing the site's history (a barn constructed on the 7348 Hayden Run Road property in 1900, the residence and three grain mills constructed between 1950 and 1951, and a house and barn constructed on the 7328 Hayden Run Road property in 1900, with the owners acquiring the properties in 2025 and 2023, respectively); surrounding land uses in Brown Township and the City of Columbus, consisting of automotive and park space to the north, agricultural uses to the south, a future mixed-use development to the west, and residential and automotive uses to the east; and conformity with the Brown Township Comprehensive Plan (2024), which identifies the property as low density/intensity, intended for residential and a small amount of low-impact commercial use in a single-use structure, and recommends 30 percent lot coverage, a maximum height of 25 feet, and a setback of between 30 and 50 feet. Mr. Workman summarized the applicant's development standards submitted under Section 420.034 of the Franklin County Zoning Resolution, including personal storage and office use in five total one- to two-story buildings; a 6-foot-tall fence along the right-of-way; application of the Community Service district development standards under Section 332.04; replacement of trees that die within 30 days, weather permitting; landscaping along the Hayden Run Road frontage with evergreen and deciduous shade trees; no obnoxious displays; a single 20-foot-wide curb cut on Hayden Run Road; and a below-ground storm drainage network designed so that 5 of 115 drainage and runoff do not cause damage to off-site areas, in compliance with the Franklin County Stormwater Drainage Manual. The applicant requested compliance waivers to allow side-yard setbacks of 20 feet along the northern and western property lines, 10 feet along the eastern property line, and 100 feet along the front edge; to waive the screening and opacity requirements; to allow two parking spaces and one ADA-compliant parking ramp space; to reduce loading spaces to zero; to allow a 6-foot-high fence along the right-of-way set back 5 feet from Hayden Run Road; to allow a minimum 10-foot screening setback along the side yard; and to allow 80 percent lot coverage. Mr. Workman summarized review comments received following referral to the Informal Technical Review Committee on September 22, 2026, from the Franklin County Engineer's Office (Hayden Run Road is a minor arterial with a recommended right-of-way width of 100 feet; dedication of right-of-way by quitclaim deed to the Franklin County Commissioners to achieve 50 feet along the front edge; an updated, stamped sight-distance exhibit with a decision point measured 18 feet from the edge of the traveled way and a sight-distance triangle of 500 feet in each direction; and compliance of pedestrian and bicycle facilities with the Engineer's Office shared-use path standards), the Franklin County Drainage Engineer's Office (a system of catch basins and storm sewers conveying stormwater to an underground detention system outletting to an existing 30-inch storm sewer in the Hayden Run Road right-of-way, with a detailed site improvement plan and final stormwater management report required with the Certificate of Zoning Compliance), the Franklin County Economic Development and Planning Department (extension of screening along the eastern property line), and Brown Township (concerns regarding the location of the proposed rezoning and the self-storage use; the Select Commercial Planned District is not included in the township's proposed zoning resolution to be voted upon at the November general election; the use does not align with the Brown Township Comprehensive Plan; and the township is interested in other options for the property, including a Type 1 annexation into the City of Columbus, affordable housing, or a park or additional green space). Staff found the rezoning consistent with the comprehensive plan's recommendation for a lowimpact use in terms of traffic generation, but noted that the proposed number of buildings is not consistent with the plan's bulk and dimensional recommendation of one single-use structure, and that the proposed 80 percent lot coverage is not consistent with the plan's recommended 30 percent lot coverage, although it is consistent with the Community Service district development standards. Staff noted that urban residential developments exist within a half mile of the property and that the property to the west is a proposed mixed-use development in the City of Columbus, including single-family ranch homes and townhomes, apartments, and commercial uses, with townhomes abutting the subject property. Staff found the rezoning generally consistent with the area and was supportive of the proposed land use and of the requested waivers for the fence along the right-of-way, screening for portions of the perimeter fencing facing the Hayden Run Road frontage, and reduced parking and loading spaces. Regarding the requested 10-foot setback 6 of 115 on the eastern boundary, staff recommended increased screening and noted that the Board of Commissioners may impose increased screening and/or buffering in that area. Staff Recommendation Staff recommended conditional approval of the rezoning from the Rural (R) district to the Select Commercial Planned District (SCPD) for a personal self-storage complex, subject to the following conditions: (1) additional screening along the eastern property boundary in the form of landscaping, solid/opaque fencing, or a combination thereof; (2) provision of additional right-ofway to meet the Franklin County Thoroughfare Plan's recommended half-width of 50 feet from the centerline; (3) provision of a 10-foot-wide shared-use path, to be approved by the Franklin County Engineer's Office and shown on the site improvement plan submitted with the Certificate of Zoning Compliance; (4) prior to issuance of the Certificate of Zoning Compliance, submission of a freshly engineered, stamped, and signed sight-distance exhibit for review and acceptance by the Franklin County Engineer's Office; and (5) prior to consideration by the Franklin County Board of Commissioners, revision of the development plan to identify the location and type of screening and fencing proposed, with all Technical Review Committee comments requesting site plan revisions to be addressed. Comments In response to questions from Mr. Hoye, Mr. Fitzpatrick explained that the plan was initially submitted without a stormwater management plan providing calculations, raising questions regarding collection volumes, storage capacity, and discharge to the roadside ditch, but that the applicant subsequently coordinated with the Engineer's Office, which found the proposed method of stormwater management sufficient to avoid damage. Mr. Fitzpatrick stated that the existing houses are served by individual wells, which would be abandoned in favor of a new well serving the office and any fire-suppression needs, and that the site is not connected to city sewer. In response to a question from Ms. Owens, Mr. Fitzpatrick explained that, until Brown Township adopts its own zoning through the election and certification process, the County maintains zoning and land-use authority and will process applications within those boundaries; upon certification of a vote adopting township zoning, zoning authority would transfer to the township. In response to questions from Mr. Blechschmidt, Mr. Workman stated that there is no objective means of measuring the proposed standard prohibiting obnoxious displays, which could be referenced to the County's signage code prohibiting displays such as flashing signs or attentionseeking devices; Mr. Hoye noted that Brown Township may have a standard with which the applicant might have to comply. Mr. Fitzpatrick stated that the Engineer's Office will consider sight distance for the proposed fence, that the compliance waiver is required because a 6-foot fence is not otherwise permitted between a principal structure and the right-of-way, that the proposed wrought-iron-type fence is largely see-through from the roadway, and that any portion within the sight visibility triangles would need to be removed or relocated. Mr. Workman noted 7 of 115 that the fence designs were included in the packet and that the aluminum picket-style fence would front the Hayden Run Road right-of-way. In response to questions from Mr. Hoye regarding the house to the east of the site, Mr. Workman stated that the house is owned not by the developer but by the owner of the industrial site to its east. Mr. Fitzpatrick stated that notice of the application and of the hearing was sent to all surrounding property owners in accordance with the notification requirements of the Ohio Revised Code, and that staff had received no response from and had no direct dialogue with that property owner. No representative of the township appeared regarding this application. Chairman Chaney noted that Brown Township had submitted an email, summarized in the staff report under the Technical Review Committee comments, outlining its concerns and respectfully requesting a postponement. Mr. Fitzpatrick stated that staff responded to the email to inform the township of the County's statutory requirements to process rezoning applications. Jack Reynolds, Esq., appeared on behalf of the applicant, Smith and Hale, 172 East State Street, Columbus, Ohio. Mr. Reynolds described the proposal as a typical self-storage facility of oneand two-story buildings with a small office, with the buildings forming facades for security and fencing provided where buildings do not connect. He stated that the fencing along the Hayden Run Road frontage is well behind the right-of-way and will not create sight-distance concerns, that a sight-line study for the curb cut was submitted with the application, that the stormwater detention plan had been submitted and resolved with the county engineer, and that the applicant is willing to add the trees requested by staff along the eastern boundary. Mr. Reynolds stated that the house abutting the site to the east is owned by the family that owns the adjacent automobile repair facility, which has been in discussion with the applicant. He reported that the applicant had consulted the Ohio EPA regarding a contained, monitored septic tank for the office, subject to Ohio EPA inspection, and that the City of Columbus was not interested in annexing the property for self-storage use. In response to questions from Mr. Hoye, Mr. Reynolds stated that the existing septic systems would be abandoned, that the new system would be a contained tank, and that a new well would be dug. Mr. Reynolds confirmed the applicant's agreement to all five conditions recommended by staff. In response to a comment from Chairman Chaney regarding planned apartments to the west, Mr. Reynolds described the self-storage use as an appropriate transition between the multifamily use to the west and the automobile repair facility to the east. No member of the public appeared to speak regarding this application. Mr. Blechschmidt raised a concern regarding enforcement of the obnoxious-display standard and asked whether a sixth condition was warranted. In response to a question from Chairman Chaney, Mr. Fitzpatrick explained that a jurisdiction adopting its own zoning also adopts a zoning map, and that, should this application be approved prior to Brown Township adopting 8 of 115 zoning but the use not be implemented, the zoning of the property would change to the designation on the adopted zoning map, with any resulting legal questions to be resolved between the property owner and the township; the County remains bound to process applications while it maintains zoning authority. Mr. Workman read the full text of the applicant's environmental treatment standard in Section B: “No banners, pennants, streamers or other similar obnoxious display shall be permitted on the site.” Mr. Workman and Mr. Reynolds confirmed that the staff presentation had paraphrased the applicant's self-imposed development text, and Mr. Fitzpatrick stated that staff could confer with the applicant regarding striking the word “obnoxious” and limiting the standard to the types of displays identified. Mr. Blechschmidt stated that this addressed his concerns and declined to add a condition. Motion Mr. Blechschmidt moved to approve Case No. ZON-26-11 with the five conditions outlined by staff. Mr. Hoye seconded the motion. The vote was as follows: Yeses: Bennett, Owens, Hoye, Blechschmidt (4). Nos: Mitchell, Chaney (2). The motion to recommend approval carried. Case No. JEFF-26-07 — 7945 Clark State Road, Jefferson Township Applicant/Owner: Property owner; no representative of the applicant appeared. Request: Rezoning of approximately 9.45 acres from the Countryside Suburban Residential (CSR) district to the Restricted Suburban Residential (RSR) district to allow a lot split. Staff Presentation Ms. Johnson presented the staff report, noting that the lot is served by well and septic and contains an existing residence, developed in 2017, with a driveway accessing Clark State Road to the north; that another residence and detached structure, since demolished, existed on the lot prior to 1995; and that the Farms at Jefferson subdivision, zoned Planned Residential, lies just east of the property. Ms. Johnson summarized the Jefferson Township Comprehensive Plan (adopted 2025), which recommends low-density residential uses at a maximum density of one dwelling unit per acre, with increased setbacks for a scenic aesthetic, and noted that the existing CSR district is intended for agricultural and conservation-style development, while the proposed RSR district is intended for low-density residential development. The current lot conditions meet the standards of both districts. Ms. Johnson summarized review comments from the Franklin County Engineer's Office, which stated that a shared driveway may be required between the split lot and the remainder lot due to driveway-spacing requirements under the access management regulations, and that a sightdistance exhibit is required due to existing roadway conditions. 9 of 115 Staff Recommendation Staff found no concerns and recommended approval of the request to rezone from the Countryside Suburban Residential district to the Restricted Suburban Residential district. By voice vote (Commission) 1 of 44 FRANKLIN COUNTY RURAL ZONING COMMISSION MINUTES OF MEETING Thursday, October 22, 2026 Judicial Services Building Commissioners Hearing Room, First Floor 369 South High Street, Columbus, Ohio 43215 MEMBERS PRESENT Glenn Taylor, Sr., Vice Chair James Leezer Paul Denton Tiffany Hanna Lisa Shirkey MEMBERS ABSENT Susan Brobst, Chairwoman Nancy Hunter STAFF PRESENT Raimere Fitzpatrick, Planning Administrator, Franklin County Economic Development and Planning Department Tamara Ennist, Planning Administrator, Franklin County Economic Development and Planning Department Austin Workman, Planner, Franklin County Economic Development and Planning Department Adria Fields, Assistant Prosecuting Attorney, Franklin County Prosecutor's Office OTHERS PRESENT / SPEAKERS Jack Reynolds, Esq., Smith and Hale, on behalf of the applicant (ZON-26-11) I. CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL At 1:30 p.m., Vice Chair Taylor called the meeting of the Franklin County Rural Zoning Commission to order. Before the roll was called, Vice Chair Taylor introduced and welcomed the Commission's newest members. Lisa Shirkey stated that she represents Hamilton Township, Franklin County, where she serves as fiscal officer. Paul Denton stated that he represents Pleasant Township, Franklin County, as a trustee. Tiffany Hanna stated that she represents Clinton Township as a trustee. Ms. Ennist called the roll. Present were Mr. Leezer, Ms. Shirkey, Ms. Hanna, Mr. Denton, and Vice Chair Taylor. Ms. Hunter and Chairwoman Brobst were absent. Ms. Ennist declared that a Rural Zoning Commission Minutes – October 22, 2026 – Page 1 2 of 44 quorum was present. Vice Chair Taylor noted that Chairwoman Brobst was unable to attend and that he would conduct the meeting. II. INTRODUCTION OF STAFF Mr. Fitzpatrick introduced staff: himself, Planning Administrator with Franklin County Economic Development and Planning; Tamara Ennist, Planning Administrator; Austin Workman, Planner; and Adria Fields, Assistant Prosecuting Attorney, representing the Franklin County Prosecutor's Office. III. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Vice Chair Taylor called for a motion on the minutes of the September 17, 2026, meeting. There was no discussion. Motion: Mr. Leezer moved to approve the minutes of the September 17, 2026, meeting as written. Ms. Hanna Mr. Leezer – Yes; Ms. Shirkey – Yes; Ms. Hanna – Yes; Mr. Denton – Abstain; Vice Chair Taylor – Yes Motion carried (4–0, with one abstention). The minutes were approved. Second: Roll Call Vote: Result: IV. NEW BUSINESS A. Case No. ZON-26-11 Location: Township: Acreage: Request: Staff Presenter: 7328–7348 Hayden Run Road, north side of Hayden Run Road, west/south of the Heritage Trail Brown Township 3.57 acres Rezoning from the Rural (R) district to the Select Commercial Planned District for a self-storage facility Austin Workman, Planner Staff Report. Mr. Workman reported that the property owner is requesting to rezone the property from the Rural district to the Select Commercial Planned District for a self-storage facility. The properties were developed from the early 1900s through 1951, and the owners acquired the property in 2023 and 2025. Surrounding properties are located in both Brown Township and the City of Columbus and include rural, high-density mixed use, and light industrial uses. Hayden Place, a high-density mixed-use development, is located directly to the west of the subject property. The property is subject to the Brown Township Comprehensive Plan (2024), which recommends the property for low density/intensity. Intended uses include residential, a small amount of Rural Zoning Commission Minutes – October 22, 2026 – Page 2 3 of 44 commercial located in a single-use structure, and low-impact uses. The plan recommends 30 percent lot coverage, a maximum height of 25 feet, and a setback of between 30 and 50 feet. The rezoning is not consistent with the dimensional standards recommended by the plan but is generally consistent with its use recommendations. The Select Commercial Planned District submittal requires identification of existing and proposed development features under Section 420.034 of the Franklin County Zoning Resolution. The proposed permitted uses include a personal self-storage use consisting of five one- to two-story buildings plus an office, and a 6-foot-tall fence along the right-of-way. The development standards of the Community Service district, as outlined in Section 332.04 of the Zoning Resolution, will apply. The applicant requested the following compliance waivers: 1. A side-yard setback of 20 feet along the northern and western property lines, 10 feet along the eastern property line, and 100 feet along the frontage; 2. A waiver of the screening and opacity requirements, as shown on the site plan; 3. Two parking spaces, one ADA space, and zero loading spaces; 4. A 6-foot-high fence along the right-of-way, set back 5 feet from the road; 5. A minimum 10-foot screening setback along the side yard; and 6. 80 percent lot coverage. The development text further provides that fencing shown on the plan will be maintained at its current height for security reasons; that no banners, pennants, streamers, or other obnoxious displays will be permitted on the site; and that there will be only one 25-foot-wide curb cut. The applicant has provided a below-grade storm-drainage network to capture and convey runoff through a series of inlets. Agency comments were as follows: Franklin County Engineer's Office: Requirements for right-of-way dedication, a sight distance exhibit, and pedestrian/bicycle facilities in the shared-use path are to be addressed during the zoning compliance phase. A detailed site improvement plan and final stormwater management report will be required as part of the Certificate of Zoning Compliance and must comply with the Franklin County Stormwater Drainage Manual. Franklin County Economic Development and Planning: Expressed concerns regarding screening along the eastern property line and requested that screening be extended in this area. Brown Township: Expressed concerns with the location of the proposed rezoning and the self-storage use. The Select Commercial Planned District is not included in the Township's proposed zoning resolution, which will be voted upon at the November general election. The Township does not believe the use aligns with the Brown Township Comprehensive Plan and is interested in exploring other options for the property, including annexation into the City of Columbus, a possible location for affordable housing, or a park or additional greenspace. Rural Zoning Commission Minutes – October 22, 2026 – Page 3 4 of 44 Staff found that the rezoning is consistent with the Comprehensive Plan's recommendation of lowimpact use in terms of use and traffic generation. The proposed number of buildings is not consistent with the plan's bulk and dimensional recommendations, as the plan recommends one single-use structure. The proposed 80 percent lot coverage is not consistent with the plan's recommendation of 30 percent coverage; however, 80 percent coverage is consistent with the Community Service district development standards. The surrounding properties are characterized by a mix of planned urban residential and commercial densities to the west, agricultural and low-density residential uses to the south, and industrial uses developed with automotive uses to the east. Urban residential developments are located within a half mile of the property. The property to the west is a proposed mixed-use development in the City of Columbus that will include single-family ranch homes and townhomes, apartments, and commercial uses, with the townhomes abutting the subject property. Staff found that the proposed rezoning and use are consistent with the area and is supportive of the proposed land uses. Staff is supportive of the requested compliance waivers, including the 6-foot-tall fence along the right-of-way, the screening and opacity requirements for the perimeter fence, and the reduced number of parking and loading spaces. Regarding the 10-foot setback along the eastern property boundary, staff recommends increased screening and noted that the Board of Commissioners may impose increased screening and/or buffering in this location. No review agencies expressed concerns with the proposed use, but concerns were raised regarding screening and buffering along the eastern property line. Staff recommended that the Rural Zoning Commission conditionally approve the request to rezone from the Rural (R) district to the Select Commercial Planned District for a personal self-storage facility, subject to the following conditions: 1. Additional screening shall be provided along the eastern property boundary in the form of landscaping or solid opaque fencing, or a combination thereof. 2. Additional right-of-way shall be provided to meet the Franklin County Thoroughfare Plan recommendation, with right-of-way 50 feet from centerline. 3. A 10-foot-wide shared-use path shall be provided, to be approved by the Franklin County Engineer's Office and shown on the site improvement plan submitted with the Certificate of Zoning Compliance application. 4. Prior to issuance of any Certificate of Zoning Compliance, the applicant must submit a professionally engineered, stamped, and signed sight distance exhibit for review and acceptance by the Franklin County Engineer's Office. 5. Prior to consideration by the Franklin County Board of Commissioners, the development plan must be revised to identify the location and type of screen fencing proposed, and all TRC comments and plan revisions must be addressed. There were no questions of staff from the Commission. No Township presentation was made. Rural Zoning Commission Minutes – October 22, 2026 – Page 4 5 of 44 Applicant Testimony. Jack Reynolds, attorney with Smith and Hale, 172 East State Street, Columbus, Ohio, appeared on behalf of the applicant. Mr. Reynolds stated that, although there had been discussion of possibly annexing the property into the City of Columbus, the applicant wished to develop the property in the township. He stated that the proposed self-storage facility, located between the large multifamily and commercial development to the west and an auto repair shop to the east, would serve as an accessory use to the development to the west, and that the applicant chose the Select Commercial Planned District to bring the request before the Commission. Mr. Reynolds stated that the applicant had been in contact with the property owners and developer to the west and with the auto repair facility to the east, neither of whom objected to the rezoning. He stated that the applicant had met with staff, agrees with staff's recommendations, and intends to add as much landscaping as possible to create an attractive addition to the Hayden Run Road corridor, noting that self-storage facilities are typically very low impact on abutting property owners. Commission Discussion. Mr. Denton asked whether there would be any restrictions on the contents stored in the units, referencing a prior incident on the east side of Columbus in which explosives stored in a storage unit resulted in a large fire and an evacuation. Mr. Reynolds stated that the owners would restrict such storage and that the leases would specifically state that those types of items cannot be stored in the units. At the request of Vice Chair Taylor, Mr. Workman stated that staff can place conditions on the types of materials stored and that staff has seen similar restrictions in past cases prohibiting hazardous and explosive materials. Mr. Fitzpatrick confirmed that the incident referenced involved a storage facility off of Grove Road. He stated that conditions such as a prohibition on the storage of hazardous or explosive materials could be imposed, but that enforceability should be considered; any suspected storage of such materials would be referred to law enforcement or other agencies with the capacity to investigate, and staff would proceed on the assumption that patrons would be law-abiding and that the operator would have procedures in place. Mr. Reynolds stated that the applicant had no objection to including lease language prohibiting the storage of explosive or hazardous materials within the units and would rely on police and fire officials to investigate any criminal activity. Mr. Denton stated that he did not believe additional conditions were necessary and was satisfied that the applicant's commitment was on the record. Vice Chair Taylor asked whether anyone in the audience wished to speak. No one came forward. There was no further discussion from the Commission. Motion: Mr. Leezer moved to recommend conditional approval of the request to rezone from the Rural district to the Select Commercial Planned District for a personal-storage complex, subject to Conditions 1 through 5 as presented by staff and the Planning Rural Zoning Commission Minutes – October 22, 2026 – Page 5 6 of 44 Commission, with the additional condition that no hazardous materials or explosive materials be stored in the facilities. Mr. Denton Mr. Leezer – Yes; Ms. Shirkey – Yes; Ms. Hanna – Yes; Mr. Denton – Yes; Vice Chair Taylor – Yes Motion carried (5–0). The Commission recommended conditional approval, subject to Conditions 1 through 5 and the additional condition prohibiting the storage of hazardous and explosive materials. Second: Roll Call Vote: Result: V. OTHER BUSINESS There was no other new business or old business to come before the Commission. VI. ADJOURNMENT Vice Chair Taylor adjourned the meeting to November 19, 2026. The proceedings concluded at 1:56 p.m. ___ Chair/Vice Chair ___ Date Approved Franklin County Rural Zoning Commission Rural Zoning Commission Minutes – October 22, 2026 – Page 6 7 of 44 STAFF REPORT Rural Zoning Commission November 19th, 2026 Case: ZON-26-10 Prepared by: Austin Workman I. Summary Owner/Applicant: Agent: Township: Site: Acreage: Utilities: Request: Recommendation: II. • • • • • Union 911 LLC/Hounddogs Towing Jackson B. Reynolds III Franklin Township 1945 Jackson Road (PID # 140-003010, 140-004361, 140-004363, & 140-004362) 3.26 acres Private water and wastewater Requesting to rezone from the Limited Industrial (LI) to the Select Commercial Planned District (SCPD) for a towing, automobile repair, automobile sales, and contracting business. Staff recommend conditional approval Property Background/History The property was zoned LM (Limited Manufacturing) prior to 1976. A 2007 amendment to the Franklin County Zoning Resolution changed the name of the district to the current Limited Industrial (LI). 2016 – Code violation was issued and subsequent Commercial Zoning Compliance was denied for a proposed automotive repair. 2017 – Commercial Zoning Compliance, Change of Use, was approved for printing, glass blowing, and warehousing (auction items) land uses on-site. 2022 – a rezoning was applied for and later withdrawn to rezone from the Limited Industrial (LI) district to the Select Commercial Planned (SCPD) district for a range of automobile, studio, landscaping, and retail land uses. 2023 – Commercial Zoning Compliance was applied for a multi-use facility onsite inclusive of land uses permitted under the Limited Industrial (LI) district. The permit has since remained open with unresolved reviews. 150 South Front Street, FSL Suite 10 Columbus, Ohio 43215-7104 Tel: 614-525-3094 | Fax: 614-525-7155 | Development.FranklinCountyOhio.gov Planning Commission Staff Report 8 of 44 III. Surrounding Land Use/Zoning Location Jurisdiction Zoning Land Use North South Columbus; Franklin Twp. West Columbus Rural (R), Restricted Urban Residential (R-8) Manufacturing Railroad, vacant Mobile home; Singlefamily residential, automobile service Single-family residential Vacant, railroad IV. Comprehensive Plan The Southwest Area Plan (2009) recommends the property for “Light Industrial”. Business uses located within this category are “non-hazardous, low intensity industrial uses”. This includes “light manufacturing, assembling and processing, warehousing and distribution, and mixed business parks”. The corresponding zoning districts are the Restricted Industrial (RI) and the Planned Industrial Park (PIP) districts. Land Use Policy C of the Plan highlights the preservation of industrial spaces for targeted and clustered redevelopment (pg. 59). ‘Urban Design Standards Policy A’ recommends holding commercial sites to a high standard for their compatibility and blending with existing land uses nearby. text: PROPOSED AMENDMENT TO THE ROSS ESTATES PRD REGULATION TEXT Subarea B · Berlin Township, Delaware County, Ohio Property: 2174 Peachblow Road, Lewis Center, OH 43035 Parcel: 41834001049001 (Subarea B, ±1.039 ac) Amends: Ross Estates PRD Regulation Text (Books 1 and 2, dated October 3, 2025), Sections III.A.1 and III.B Purpose: (1) Increase the density of Subarea B; (2) add an accessory dwelling unit as a permitted use in Subarea B Legend: Struck-through text is deleted. Underlined bold text is added. All other text is unchanged. SECTION III.A.1 — PERMITTED USES Within this PRD, permitted uses shall be limited to the following: a. Single Family detached residential dwelling units, per Section 11.03(A), and b. Common Area, per Section 11.03(B), and c. Natural Area, per Section 11.03(C), and d. Schools, per Section 11.03(E), and e. Temporary Structures, per Section 11.03(H), and f. Casual sale of goods, per Section 11.03(I), and g. Limited home occupations, per Section 11.03(J), and h. Accessory structures and uses incidental to the principal buildings or uses, and i. Entry features; including columns, posts, signage and other elements related to community and neighborhood entrances., and j. Within Subarea B only, one (1) accessory dwelling unit, subject to Section III.B.2. SECTION III.B.1 — MAXIMUM DENSITY Maximum Density: the maximum number of dwellings shall not exceed sixty-two (62)three (63) dwelling units within the PRD boundary. This density is further limited to the following: a. Zero (0) dwellings are permitted in Subarea A, and b. A maximum of one (1) dwelling is two (2) dwelling units are permitted in Subarea B: one (1) single-family dwelling and one (1) accessory dwelling unit. SECTION III.B.2 — ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT, SUBAREA B (NEW) An accessory dwelling unit in Subarea B is a second, subordinate dwelling unit, with its own living, sleeping, cooking and sanitary facilities, on the same lot as the single-family dwelling. It shall comply with the following: 1. It shall be located within the detached accessory building existing on the parcel as of the effective date of this amendment. The building's footprint shall not be enlarged to accommodate it. 2. The owner of record shall occupy either the single-family dwelling or the accessory dwelling unit as a primary residence. 3. It shall not be sold, conveyed or subdivided separately from the single-family dwelling. 4. It shall not be rented for periods of less than thirty (30) consecutive days. 5. A minimum of two (2) off-street parking spaces shall be provided for it, in addition to those required for the single-family dwelling. 6. It shall be served by public water and public sanitary sewer, and shall comply with the Residential Code of Ohio. 7. The accessory building may also be used for uses incidental to the principal residence, including private recreation by residents and their guests (such as a pool house), storage and garage. The building shall not be used or rented for commercial events. 8. A plot plan illustrating the floor plan of the accessory dwelling unit and the proposed parking arrangement shall be submitted to obtain a zoning certificate prior to construction and building approval. All other provisions of the Ross Estates PRD Regulation Text remain unchanged. INTRODUCTION AND REQUEST This Conditional Use Permit Application Narrative has been prepared on behalf of the property owners, Erica F. Wares and James S. Wares, and the operator, Idyllvale, in support of an application to the Harlem Township Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) for a conditional use permit on approximately 15.549 acres at 5080 Harlem Road, Harlem Township, Delaware County, Ohio. The property is zoned AR-1, Agricultural Residential District, and will remain zoned AR-1. The application is submitted under Section 7.04 and Article XXVIII (Board of Zoning Appeals), Section 28.07, of the Harlem Township Zoning Resolution. Idyllvale is a nature-centered working farm and community gathering place focused on agriculture, environmental stewardship and outdoor experiential learning. Its program includes seasonal agricultural education for children and adults, a seasonal summer farm and nature day camp, and outdoor wellness and day retreat programs, all incidental to the working farm, and, in a later phase, a multi-use building, the Meadow Room at Idyllvale, that also hosts farm-centered gatherings and events. The Request. The Applicant requests a conditional use permit under Section 7.04(H) of the Zoning Resolution, which permits in the AR-1 district, as a conditional use, "public or private golf courses, country clubs, hunt clubs, fishing lakes, campgrounds or similar recreational uses, with all buildings and club houses incidental thereto, including restaurant(s) to serve members and/or users of the facility." The Applicant asks the Board to find that Idyllvale, a nature-based farm recreation, camp and outdoor education facility, is a similar recreational use, and that the Meadow Room at Idyllvale is a clubhouse incidental to that use. Specifically, the Applicant requests that the Board: • approve the conditional use described in Part IV, subject to the operating limits and proposed conditions of approval in Part X; • designate the permit as permanent and running with the land, as Section 7.04 allows, so that it does not become void on a sale or conveyance of the property (including a transfer to an ownership entity); • find that the conditional use commences with the start of Phase 1 program operations, and approve the phasing schedule in Section 4.2 for the Meadow Room at Idyllvale. Most of the Idyllvale program is agriculture, which Ohio law exempts from township zoning, or agritourism, which a township may regulate only in narrow respects (ORC 519.21). The seasonal farm tours, school field trips, agricultural education and summer farm camp are agritourism incidental to the working farm, and this application does not waive those protections. The conditional use is sought principally to allow the Meadow Room at Idyllvale and gatherings and events of fifty (50) or more participants, which are not agritourism. The seasonal programs, camp and day retreats are described and included so that all activity on the property that may fall outside the agricultural exemption is covered by one permit with clear, enforceable conditions. Appendix A classifies each element of the program. VOTE: HARLEM TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES Delaware County, Ohio RESOLUTION NO. 26-1118T-xxx RESOLUTION FINDING THAT DRAINAGE IMPROVEMENTS BENEATH TWO PRIVATE DRIVEWAYS ADJACENT TO HARLEM TOWNSHIP PARK SERVE A PUBLIC PURPOSE, AND AUTHORIZE TOWNSHIP ADMINISTRATOR TO OBTAIN ENGINEERING PLANS, CONSTRUCTION QUOTES, AND PROPERTY OWNER AGREEMENTS FOR BOARD REVIEW WHEREAS, Harlem Township (the "Township") owns and operates Harlem Township Park (the "Park"), the Township Administration Building, the Township Fire Station, and the parking areas serving those facilities (together, the "Township Facilities"), located on and adjacent to State Route 605; and WHEREAS, stormwater from around the Administration Building and Fire Station drains beneath State Route 605 through an existing culvert and directly into the Park, and from the Park flows westward beneath two privately owned driveways adjacent to the Park; and WHEREAS, the Township retained Coldwater Consulting, LLC ("Coldwater") to evaluate flooding affecting the Township Facilities, and Coldwater presented its Harlem Township Flooding Evaluation to this Board on or about September 16, 2026; and WHEREAS, Coldwater identified a crushed culvert at a driveway west of the Park that reduces downstream conveyance capacity, and found that the blocked driveway and adjacent driveway causes drainage backup, overtops the driveways, contributes to upstream flooding; and WHEREAS, Coldwater documented flooding of the Township Administration Building parking lot, the Park and playground, including the Park's southern boundary, during the rain event of August 11, 2026. Its hydraulic model estimated runoff volumes west of State Route 605 of 1.6 acre-feet in a 1-year storm and 4.0 acre-feet in a 10-year storm; and WHEREAS, Coldwater recommended that the Township "fix the conveyance problem by replacing the culverts under the driveway downstream," noting that removing this restriction can lower the system water level by approximately one to two feet and reduce the volume of water backing up into the Township parking lot; and WHEREAS, the existing drainage structures beneath the two driveways are not capable of accommodating the volume of stormwater draining from the Park, and the resulting restriction contributes to annual flooding and damage within the Park and causes stormwater to accumulate in the parking lot serving the Administration Building and Fire Station; and WHEREAS, during a 10-year or 25-year rain event, the existing drainage limitations could result in flooding of and damage to the Fire Station and Administration Building, interrupting fire, emergency medical, and administrative services to township residents; and WHEREAS, the owners of the affected private properties have verbally indicated their willingness to consent to the Township's entry onto their properties and to the construction of the proposed improvements; and WHEREAS, the Township's special counsel has provided this Board with a written legal opinion concluding that the expenditure of Township funds for drainage improvements on private property necessary to protect the Administration Building and parking lot, Fire Station, and Park, serves a proper public purpose, is authorized under the foregoing statutes, and has recommended that the Board adopt a resolution expressly identifying the public facilities and services protected, the engineering findings supporting the project, the necessity of performing limited work on private property, and the incidental nature of any private benefit; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Trustees of Harlem Township, Delaware County, Ohio, that: Section 1. Public Facilities and Services Protected. The Board finds that the proposed drainage improvements are intended to protect the following Township-owned public property and services: the Township Administration Building; the Township Fire Station; Harlem Township Park and its playground; the parking areas serving those facilities; and the uninterrupted delivery of fire, emergency medical, administrative and park services to the residents of Harlem Township. Section 2. Engineering Findings. The Board adopts the recitals above as findings of fact and finds, based on the evaluation and recommendations of Coldwater Consulting, LLC that the undersized and damaged culverts beneath the two driveways adjacent to the Park are a hydraulic restriction within the drainage system serving the Township Facilities, and that increasing their capacity is expected to significantly reduce recurring flooding of the Administration Building parking lot and Park and to substantially reduce the risk of flood damage to the Park, Fire Station and Administration Building during a 10-year or 25-year rain event. Section 3. Necessity of Limited Work on Private Property. The Board finds that the hydraulic restriction is physically located beneath the two privately owned driveways, that the restriction cannot be corrected by work on Township property alone, and that the location of the work on private property is dictated by the engineering solution and is incidental to it. The work on private property shall be limited to what is reasonably necessary to restore drainage capacity serving the Township Facilities. Section 4. Incidental Private Benefit. The Board finds that the primary objective and dominant purpose of the project is the protection and maintenance of Township Facilities and the continuity of public services, and that it is required for the general good of all inhabitants of the Township. Any benefit to the owners of the affected private properties, including the replacement of culverts beneath their driveways, is incidental to that public purpose. The project is not a private improvement project. Section 5. Determination of Public Purpose and Statutory Authority. Based on the findings in Sections 1 through 4, the Board, in the exercise of its legislative discretion, determines that spending Township funds on the survey, engineering design, and construction of the drainage improvements described in this resolution serves a proper public purpose and is within the Township's statutory authority. Ohio Revised Code §505.37(A) expressly authorizes the Township to spend funds to care for and maintain fire equipment and buildings. Ohio Revised Code §§511.11, 505.21, and 505.261 authorize the Township to acquire, construct, and maintain administrative offices and parks. These express powers necessarily include reasonable measures needed to preserve the usefulness of those facilities. Section 6. Engineering Authorization. The Township Administrator is authorized to accept and execute, on behalf of the Township, agreements of $10,000 or less for professional engineering services to design a plan to remedy the drainage restrictions below the private driveways. Section 7. Construction Quotes. Upon completion of the engineering plans, the Township Administrator is authorized to solicit quotes or bids for construction of the drainage improvements in accordance with the plans and applicable Ohio competitive bidding requirements, and to present the results to the Board. Section 8. Property Owner Agreements. The Township Administrator is authorized to work with the Township’s special counsel to prepare written agreements with the owners of the affected private properties providing for (a) the owners' written consent to the Township's entry onto their properties and the construction of improvements, (b) any temporary easements needed, and (c) such other terms as counsel recommends. Such agreements shall be presented to the Board for approval and shall be executed by the trustees before any construction begins. Section 9. No Construction Authorized. Nothing in this resolution authorizes construction. Construction may proceed only after the Board, by further resolution, has reviewed the final engineering plans, construction quotes, and executed property owner agreements, and has authorized the construction expenditure. Section 10. Effective Date. This resolution shall take effect immediately upon its adoption. Trustee [___] moved the adoption of the foregoing resolution, and Trustee [___] seconded the motion. Upon roll call, the vote was as follows: Adopted this 18th day of November, 2026. HARLEM TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES ___, Trustee Adam Holliday ___, Trustee Jon Trainer ___, Trustee Robert Singer
